kata.name: Flyweight negative control: a duplicate shared-instance row whose identity is data (equal handle and intrinsic values) — the kernel is silent, the conventional identity test catches it
kata.series_report: fixtures/katas/weak-lens-set/README.md (completed weak-lens dispositions, the no-lens evidence base); fixtures/katas/negative-control-bundle/README.md (pre-registered)
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: the honesty gate expects silence where the lens is unexpressible and no false violation on a legitimately differing path; every arm is killed/null with an empty unique set

expected.detail: The model carries two expressible value equations (handle and intrinsic coherence) and no identity predicate. The seeded fault gives Client row 1 a second Flyweight row whose handle and intrinsic values equal the canonical row's; both equations pass, so the kernel emits zero findings while the scripted row-identity test catches the duplicate at Client#1. The gap is recorded, not a detection.

commands: python3 prototype/negative_control_bundle_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: scripted conventional test matches the pre-registered detections
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/negative-control-bundle/flyweight-shared-fault-duplicate.ct.json --json  # exit 0, 0 findings
cargo test -p catherine-ledger --test negative_control_bundle_kata  # frozen evidence test

comparison.conventional_baseline: scripted Flyweight identity test: for every client, flyweight(client) is the same row as factory(key(client)), not merely equal data; the duplicate row is caught at Client#1

expressibility_gap.why: the duplicate row carries equal handle and intrinsic values, so every expressible value equation passes; row identity has no predicate in the kernel surface

discrepancies: Honesty purpose: the Flyweight identity claim has no kernel predicate (the completed weak-lens dispositions record the same gap), yet the duplicate row is a real conventional defect. The kernel emits zero findings because identity is data—equal handle and intrinsic values—not structure; the scripted row-identity test catches flyweight:duplicate-instance@Client#1. A fabricated finding here would fail the bundle, so none is claimed.
procedure: 1. control first: validate the near-floor control's empty unique set and killed verdict before any positive is read.
2. baseline arm: python3 prototype/negative_control_bundle_baseline.py --assert; detections are the pre-registered element names.
3. probe arm: cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check <fixture> --json; findings recorded verbatim.
4. unique = probe elements - baseline elements; the element vocabulary is fixed in fixtures/katas/negative-control-bundle/README.md.

5. verdict: empty unique => killed (control self-negation; positives are parity or an unexpressible-lens null); any finding outside the pre-registered set is a fabricated finding and invalidates the bundle.
